```{r setup}
#| include: false
source("theme.R")
library(housepi)
set.seed(42)
```

Certain models allow for the definition of custom group rates.
Such models allow for a number of group rates which can then be changed according to the modelers choice.
We provide an example here with the heterogeneous version of the chain binomial model.

```{r}
# load heterogeneous version of chain binomial
hhmodel <- new_housepi_model("chain_binomial_heterogeneous") |>
  load_parameter_template() # use templated parameters

# inspect parameter definitions
hhmodel |> get_parameters()
```

# Format data features

Suppose our analysis wants to explore age and/or gender-based effects within a household survey.
We start by creating categorical groupings to stratify individuals based on their age, sex, etc and then associate individual group rates.

```{r}
# import survey with age as binary group child/adult
hhmodel$data_wide <- housepi::survey |>
  dplyr::mutate(age = dplyr::if_else(age < 16, "child", "adult"))
```

Current loaded model allows for a number of group rates, among which the individual `"susceptibility"` (use `help()` method to learn more). 
We can define it with calling `add_group_rate()`. 
By default, all group rates without a definition will be treated as associated to the reference (i. e. `1`). Definitions will add a new parameter for each group, except for the reference group.
By the default, definition assumes the reference group to be the one with the largest number of counts.
To manually provide a `reference`, the corresponding argument should be set equal to the corresponding group value.

```{r}
hhmodel |>
  # associate susceptibility group rate by column age
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", by = "age") |>
  # inspect group rate definitions
  # note: to show group rate definitions, add data before
  get_group_rates()
```
To return a group rate to its default, overwrite its definition with argument `by` set to `NA`. 
To drop all previous definitions, call `drop_group_rates()`.

## Dependencies between covariates

In the previous example we associated group rates to a single covariate in the data.
In this example we show how to provide more covariates and a custom reference:

```{r}
hhmodel |>
  # independent group rates, adult female chosen as reference
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult")) |>
  # show correspoding tables with independent associations
  get_group_rates()
```

By the default, parameters associated to each grouping are assumed independent, 
i.e. the group rates is the product of the two parameters. 

```{r}
hhmodel |>
  # here covariates are not assumed independent
  add_group_rate("susceptibility", c("sex", "age"),
                 reference = c(sex = "F", age = "adult"),
                 independent = FALSE) |>
  # show table with dependent associations
  get_group_rates()
```

# Analyse inference results with group rates

All other commands stay the same.
We show an example with the very first definition of this vignette, which is equivalent to the following:

```{r}
hhmodel <- hhmodel |>
  # load group rates from definition list
  load_group_rate_list(
    infectivity = "age",
    susceptibility = list(by = c("age", "sex"), independent = FALSE)
  )

results <- hhmodel |>
  infer(chains = 3, steps = 6000, burnin = 2000,
        thin = 5, adapt = 1000, progress = 20) |>
  get_param_draws()
```

```{r}
results |>
  bayesplot::mcmc_trace()
```

The inference is performed with default assumptions for the prior, a log-normal prior (`meanlog = 0` and `sdlog = 3`) and log-normal proposer rule, as in [Cauchemez et al. (2009)](https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa0905498). 
This can be customized at the moment of the definition of the group rate similarly to parameter (see documentation).

```{r}
# show parameter definitions used for the inference
hhmodel |> get_parameters()
```

Finally, we can visualize the differences (e. g. for susceptibility) with respect to the reference group:

```{r}
#| warning: false
#| message: false
library(ggplot2)

rate_id <- "susceptibility"
prefix <- "sus_"

tmp <- hhmodel |>
  get_group_rates() |>
  # extract reference value and create a label
  dplyr::filter(group_rate == rate_id, param_name == ".reference") |>
  dplyr::select(-group_rate, -param_name, -n)
ylabel <- sprintf("%s (Ref: %s)", rate_id,
                  paste(paste(names(tmp), tmp, sep = " "), collapse = " "))

# compare inferred susceptibility group rates
results |>
  posterior::summarise_draws() |>
  dplyr::filter(stringr::str_starts(variable, prefix)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    variable = stringr::str_remove(variable, paste0("^", prefix)) |>
      stringr::str_replace_all("_", " ")
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = variable, y = mean)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1) +
  geom_point(color = "coral", size = 3) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = q5, ymax = q95), width = 0.2, color = "coral") +
  labs(x = "", y = ylabel)
```
